newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Ellis targets U.S, Europe.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Ellis targets U.S, Europe.

text.p: British-based chemicals distribution company Ellis & Everard Plc on Monday signalled it was targeting further acquisitions in the U.S. and Europe, as well as starting to turn its attention to the developing chemicals market in Asia.
Earlier the company announced its first move into the U.S. specialty chemicals distribution market through the $21.5 million purchase of Mozel Inc, based in St Louis, Missouri.

In a telephone interview with Reuters following the announcement of a 16 percent rise in full-year pre-tax profit to 29.6 million stg, chief executive Peter Wood said the group's strategy over the past five years had delivered "growth in all the key numbers in double digits, and we believe we have the momentum to take that further."

Wood said Ellis & Everard was more likely to continue to seek small bolt-on acquisitions in line with the six businesses purchased in the past 18 months. But he said that with interest cover of more than ten times, "we believe we have the financial capacity to gear up."

The Mozel acquisition lifted Ellis & Everard to fourth place in the fragmented U.S. chemical distribution market. But Wood said "The number one has only five percent (market share) so there are a lot of opportunities for growth."

In Europe, Ellis & Everard is keen to move into the major French and German markets, but Wood said distribution companies in Europe were performing relatively poorly and he was not prepared to overpay.
"In the long term we see opportunities looking further afield and we are starting to be aware of the Far East," he added.

Increasing restructuring in the chemicals industry was highlighted by news earlier Monday that Britain's Imperial Chemical Industries Plc had sold most of its bulk chemical operations to DuPont Co of the U.S.

Wood said such changes created increasing opportunities for chemical distributors to add value, taking over responsibility for operations such as warehousing as well as managing movement of chemicals.
"We are taking on more links in the supply chain. That presents a greater raft of opportunities," he said.

Wood said the company had an "excellent relationship with DuPont," managing distribution for the U.S. group's UK nylon business. Ellis & Everard also works with the polyester business sold to DuPont by ICI on Monday.

"We have been involved with a number of businesses that have left ICI. What we are confident about is that these will be in a home where the new owner will see them as core and want them to grow and develop," said Wood.
